title: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS) — 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average, 12:00 p.m. ET, surveying the week that contains the FHFA HPI print
source: EST: TWO Freddie Mac primaries read direct 2026-10-01-forward on 2026-09-15 during the fhfa-hpi-2026-09-29 D-14 pulse-check adjacency sweep. (1) freddiemac.com/pmms (HTTP 200, 103,786 bytes) states the publisher's own standing rule verbatim: "PMMS results are released weekly on Thursdays at 12 p.m. ET. and are an average of loan rates offered the prior Thursday through Wednesday." The same page carries the live reading it anchors against — "U.S. weekly mortgage rate averages as of 09/10/2026, 30-year Fixed-Rate Mortgage 6.76%, 15-year Fixed-Rate Mortgage 6.09%". (2) freddiemac.com/pmms/docs/PMMS_Publication_Calendar.pdf (HTTP 200, 93,314 bytes), the publisher's own FORWARD-DATED publication calendar, whose row reads "Publication Date 10/1/2026 | Week Beginning 9/24/2026 | Week Ending 9/30/2026" -- extracted from the PDF by this lane itself via a pure-Python FlateDecode pass over the compressed streams (306,191 chars decoded), the same technique the fhfa-hpi-2026-09-29 initial research used on the FHFA 2026Q2 report, NOT cited second-hand. So the date is named on a forward calendar AND derivable from the publisher's stated rule. Structural corroboration from freddiemac.com/pmms/docs/PMMS_history.csv (HTTP 200, 97,403 bytes, same fetch): of 89 publication dates since 2025-01-01, 85 are Thursdays and 82 of 88 consecutive gaps are exactly 7 days; the last published row is 9/10/2026, and 9/10 + 21d = 2026-10-01. Filed estimate on taxonomy, not on date doubt: CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs (IR|CAL|BLS|FED|PJM|SEC|TSY|OCC|BEA|CENSUS|ISM|CB|UMICH|FHFA) carries no member for a GSE's own weekly survey -- the same taxonomy gap the case-shiller-hpi-2026-09-29 lane recorded for an index provider's publication rule -- and the event-research lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: THE GAP THIS PROPOSAL EXISTS TO CLOSE: across 658 tracked events the calendar carries ZERO mortgage-rate releases, while every housing ledger on the shelf names the 30-year mortgage as the live transmission channel between rates and house prices -- fhfa-hpi-2026-09-29, fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27 and fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24 all quote a PMMS reading in their base-rate sections (the 09-29 ledger's Leg 7: "the 30-year mortgage is 6.71% (2026-09-03) against 6.50% a year earlier -- the live transmission channel, tightening slightly"), and existing-home-sales, new-home-sales, housing-starts and nahb-hmi all sit in the same corridor. The number those ledgers cite has been arriving on an untracked schedule. WHY THIS EDITION RATHER THAN A BACKFILL: 2026-10-01 is the PMMS publication that falls inside fhfa-hpi-2026-09-29's own five-day corridor, and its survey week -- 9/24/2026 through 9/30/2026, per the publisher's own calendar -- BRACKETS the 2026-09-29 print itself, so it is the first mortgage reading whose measurement window contains that morning. It is also the first PMMS two full weeks after the 2026-09-16 FOMC decision, which the fomc-2026-09-16 lane read at D-1 as 91.4% priced for a HIKE. This proposal covers that one edition and does not backfill the weekly series; a lane taking it up should decide whether a weekly survey belongs on this calendar as a series or only where it brackets a tracked print. MEASURED CONTEXT AT PROPOSAL TIME, from the primaries above: 30-year FRM 6.66% (08-27) -> 6.71% (09-03) -> 6.76% (09-10), against 6.35% at 2025-09-11 -- a +41bp year-over-year gap that widened from +21bp in one week, roughly half of it base effect (the year-ago reading itself fell 6.50% -> 6.35%) rather than fresh tightening, which is stated here so a later lane does not read the whole move as new. The Treasury complex behind it repriced hawkish over the same stretch (home.treasury.gov daily par yields, fetched 2026-09-15: 2Y 4.37 -> 4.65, 10Y 4.78 -> 4.97, 30Y 5.24 -> 5.34 between 09-04 and 09-14). Impact low and symbols: [] on this lane's own re-measurement rather than inherited: no macro- or housing-keyed playbook exists in docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md or docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md (0 hits, re-grepped 2026-09-15). An estimate widens caution; nothing here licenses an entry.
